LESSON: WRITING 11.4.1 GUIDED WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to correctly write names of objects?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to write clearly and correctly is developed as they write names from picture prompts to

demonstrate mastery of vocabulary.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is promoted as the learner collaborates with others in group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills (Self- esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is enhanced as they name objects correctly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner uses the writing skills to write clearly and correctly in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,

• Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

• Pictures or picture description
